title: Saikano
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Shy Chise and awkward Shuji are high school students in a Hokkaido coastal town who have just started dating when enemy bombers strike Sapporo and Shuji discovers Chise with mechanized wings: the Self-Defense Forces have involuntarily turned her into Japan's ultimate weapon. As the weapon system overtakes her body and the war spreads, side stories follow soldiers, military spouses and bombing victims. Seven volumes, complete; published in English by Viz.
life_message: Love is what makes us human, and war and the machinery of the state destroy ordinary lives and the people caught in them.

content.note: ANN's manga review calls it a visceral war story focused on suffering and brutality; AniList War, MU War/Apocalypse.
Chise loses warmth, heartbeat and sensation and becomes a merciless force; a friend of Shuji dies (Wikipedia); ANN calls it heartbreaking.

Teen couple's sexual relationship (MU First-Time Intercourse, Nudity; ANN notes sexual attraction and cheating); Shuji's past involvement with a married woman, Fuyumi (Wikipedia). MU also lists Rape and Sexual Abuse (to verify).
Chise's dependence on medication late in the story (ANN vol. 6); no recreational use reported.
Chise's crisis over losing her humanity; Shuji's guilt; a girlfriend withdraws from school after her boyfriend's death (Wikipedia; ANN).

dominant: Anti-war tragedy; love under catastrophe; existential despair

Dignity vs honor.evidence: No honor duels; the story mourns violence rather than celebrating personal combat (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Chise and Shuji run away from military duty to live together in a bay village (ANN vol. 6).

Civic vs kin.evidence: The couple's private bond is set above the nation's war effort.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Military authority shown using a schoolgirl; reviewer notes Chise out-earns Shuji (ANN).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Secular setting; no faith or ritual frame reported.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Wartime scarcity and simple survival dominate the couple's life.

folkways.japan: Reflects Japanese postwar anti-militarism and the 'sekai-kei' pattern of a teen romance tied to the fate of the world.

delivery.evidence: ANN's volume 6 manga review says it 'lays it on a bit thick', calls it 'needlessly didactic' with characters as author mouthpieces.
delivery.note: One manga review finds the anti-war message pressed hard; a second source on delivery was not available.

winners_losers: Chise, helped by Shuji's love, reclaims her humanity and destroys her weaponized form (Wikipedia); the war still devastates the town, and sympathy goes to the couple and civilians, not the military project.
to_verify: MangaUpdates lists Rape and Sexual Abuse; no review opened confirmed the scenes or their framing.
